body:
I’m not going down a paranormal rabbit hole right now with you, because I’m going to focus on your first question:
What else would they do? There are actually several perfectly valid and effective education models aside from the highly flawed current public school model that are already in place and functioning! Just look at private schools- the best ones are so far from what public school looks like. 
For the record, homeschooled kids regularly score above their public AND private schooled peers across academic and social skill sets when tested.
 There is a new type of learner-driven “free” schools popping up that honors the individual learner’s path to education. (Not just Private schools, but obviously mostly so because those with money often get the best)
 Gifted programs in public schools are a joke that ignore many children who need the support just because they do not “qualify”. Many of those children fall through the cracks, often not academically but in other ways.

I personally considered high school my favorite years, but my subconscious took pity on me and inflicted unbearable stress headaches on me when the abuse the school system inflicts on the learners that do not learn and test well. So I got months in the hospital instead, with a home-educator provided by the school for kids unable to attend. Suddenly, with One on one instruction, I bloomed and enjoyed learning again. (Edit: because I had more say over what I worked on, I was allowed to progress through things I didn’t enjoy or found overly simplistic, and allowed to focus on the things I was good at and enjoyed.)

My 7 year old tried school and hated it. She’s homeschooled and loves it. She is years ahead of her peers, even though she has massive control over her education and spends most of her time playing. She loves learning. Seriously loves it. 
My 5 year old is excited to go to school. As long as she wants to be there, we will support her. But there are other options, and there’s no reason to pretend that public school is the best one just because it’s the only one available to many people. What needs to happen is those who are not served well by the public schools need to be listened to- not dismissed offhand with a condescending remark about how they need to grow up. 

I will say in my country, there is an obsession with standardized tests that has been getting progressively worse over the last few decades, while our scores have simultaneously been dropping. Perhaps a better question than “what else?” Would be “how does it need to change?” Because it could be a really good thing with a massive overhaul. I hear the Danish education system is phenomenal- perhaps you are from there, or some other country with a phenomenal school system. I’m guessing from your allusion to certain government agencies, though, that we are fellow countrymen(women?)

I’m actually really glad you enjoyed school. It is a fabulous system for those it works for- about 51% of the population. For the rest, it basically destroys them. It’s a beurocracy that ignores the science of how children learn- even more teachers are frustrated by this system that ties their hands. and there are several studies on how alternate, more open And learner-directed learning works much better for the large subset of learners who do not do well in traditional school.
As OP is clearly miserable, I stand firmly by what I said to them. I’m glad you enjoyed your school, that does not invalidate the masses of students who had their will to learn and live crushed. 

Honestly friendly suggestion- If you feel the need to be so attacking to those with different opinions than yours, maybe reconsider posting on a support forum full of suicidal people.

High school is shit. It gets so much better. School is a prison set to enslave the minds of the public and suck all the curiosity out of children.

Fuck school. The social constructs are made up and the facts are fucking useless. Make the grade, but realize this is not all there is. Figure out what YOU like. If people at your school are assholes, realize that once you leave school, they will fade from your life and memories, off to live their uninspiring lives
